hypotheses:
Every record the agent writes or changes is checked by a judge independent of the coding agent, against everything you said and the context you said it in, not just a quoted fragment. JEV answers first when it is confident past the threshold calibrated on your own answers; otherwise the judge model you configured answers, and one judge_model setting governs everything about verdicts. When no judge can be reached, iaso tells you once and holds only the steps that need a verdict; it never decides by fixed rules instead.
will: Judge every new or changed record, and every stale link, against your whole logged words and their context, once, on the machine that captured it; other checkouts keep that judgment (DEC-116, owner 2026-11-01).
will: Ask JEV first and the configured judge model below JEV's calibrated threshold, logging which judge gave each verdict and with what confidence.
will: Mark a judgment made on a quote alone, and never fast-track a record on it.
will: Keep JEV's provider, credential name and question form as settings, with the key never written into the repository.
will: With no judge reachable, say so once, apply the verdicts already given, and hold only what needs a verdict until a judge answers.
will: Judge code against its requirements edge by edge, weakest first, as advice, and list unjudged touched requirements at the merge.
won't: Decide any verdict by keyword, heuristic or other fixed rule, as a fallback or otherwise.
won't: Let the coding agent that wrote a record or the code be its judge.
won't: Show you the judge's doubts as a card or a read-back line to read; they reach you only as questions through the question tool.
won't: Ask you for a record id or a shell command to judge, align or set anything up.
won't: Hold your prompt, or work that needs no judge, because a judge is unreachable.
won't: Change, create or remove a link because of a fidelity judgment.
records.premise:
My intent is that most of the time the system shouldn't rely on deterministic tooling to understand intent or process text, unless we're sure the deterministic solution can handle any type of situation. Regarding intent recording. This might need a deeper brainstorming. What is the best ux to record user's intent, confirm intent is clear and completely expressed and correctly recorded?

Question: You asked, "What is the best ux to record user's intent, confirm intent is clear and completely expressed and correctly recorded?", and said it might need a deeper brainstorming. Should iaso now lock in a specific judging design (a first judge that answers when confident, a configured judge model as backup, judging only once on the machine that captured the words, and keeping your words out of the tracked repository), or should that design stay open for the brainstorm?

You said: "What is the best ux to record user's intent, confirm intent is clear and completely expressed and correctly recorded?"
Options: Leave it open for the brainstorm (Recommended) (No judging mechanism, storage location, or threshold is fixed yet. The records that fix them wait until you decide. Recommended: You said the intent recording needs a deeper brainstorm, so the specific judging mechanics were not yours to settle yet.); Adopt the described judging design (The two-stage judge, per-machine judging, and out-of-git storage become the plan. The brainstorm on the UX is then narrowed to that design.); Adopt only the judge model, not the rest (Models judge records against your words, but the threshold, per-machine rule, and storage stay open.)
Answer: Adopt the described judging design

Question: Your earlier answer was 'Only ask, never block edits', but on 2 Nov you answered 'Block only related edits'. Outside the intent loop, should an edit that would contradict or extend a confirmed record be held until you answer, or should it go ahead while the conflict is only raised as a question?

You said on 2 Nov: "Block only related edits (Recommended)"

Earlier today, asked to settle this clash, you chose "Block only related edits (2 Nov)".
Options: Block only related edits (Recommended) (An edit that contradicts or extends a confirmed record waits until you answer or a loop reaches clear intent. Other edits always go ahead. Recommended: 'Block only related edits' is your most recent answer.); Only ask, never block (Every edit goes ahead. A conflict with a confirmed record is only raised as a question.)
Answer: Block only related edits (Recommended)

Question: When the judge keeps returning answers iaso cannot use for the same record, should iaso send that case to its self-debug workflow, or should it tell you once and hold only the steps that need a verdict?

You said on date not logged: "My intent is that most of the time the system shouldn't rely on deterministic tooling to understand intent or process text, unless we're sure the deterministic solution can handle any type of situation."
Options: Tell me once and hold only the steps that need a verdict (Recommended) (Iaso reports the stuck judge to you once, waits for your answer, and decides nothing by fixed rules. It does not start the self-debug workflow on its own. Recommended: You said the system should not rely on deterministic tooling to understand intent, so keeping the decision with you and off an automatic debug path matches your words best.); Send it to the self-debug workflow first (Iaso runs its self-debug workflow on the stuck judge before it asks you anything. You only hear about it if that workflow cannot settle it.)
Answer: Tell me once and hold only the steps that need a verdict (Recommended)
